l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable

q: The Brahmans possess the privilege of teaching the Vedas, and were in former times in exclusive possession of all knowledge.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Shatriyas are warriors (the second caste)
q: from his right arm issued Shatriya (the warrior), and from his left, the warrior's wife.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Vaissyas are agriculturists and traders (the third caste)
q: His thighs produced Vaissyas, male and female (agriculturists and traders), and lastly from his feet sprang Sudras (mechanics and laborers).

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Sudras are bound to servile attendance (for the higher classes, especially Brahmans)
q: The Sudras or fourth class are bound to servile attendance on the higher classes, especially the Brahmans, but they may follow mechanical occupations and practical arts, as painting and writing, or become traders or husbandmen.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Zoroastrianism was founded or reformed by Zoroaster (as a reform of an earlier religion)
q: Zoroaster was the founder of their religion, or rather the reformer of the religion which preceded him.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pariahs are employed in lowest services (with severe social restrictions)
q: These are the Pariahs, who are employed in the lowest services and treated with the utmost severity.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pariahs are excluded from civil rights (under caste regulations)
q: They are deprived of all civil rights, and stigmatized by particular laws, regulating their mode of life, their houses and their furniture.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pariahs are considered unclean (and believed to pollute what they touch)
q: They are not only considered unclean themselves, but they render unclean every thing they touch.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Brahma's body produces Shatriyas (from the right arm)
q: Accordingly from his mouth came forth the eldest born, Brahma (the priest), to whom he confided the four Vedas; from his right arm issued Shatriya (the warrior), and from his left, the warrior's wife.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Brahma's body produces Vaissyas (from the thighs)
q: His thighs produced Vaissyas, male and female (agriculturists and traders), and lastly from his feet sprang Sudras (mechanics and laborers).

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Brahma's body produces Sudras (from the feet)
q: His thighs produced Vaissyas, male and female (agriculturists and traders), and lastly from his feet sprang Sudras (mechanics and laborers).

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Zoroastrianism was dominant in Western Asia (from the time of Cyrus until Alexander's conquest)
q: The time when he lived is doubtful, but it is certain that his system became the dominant religion of Western Asia from the time of Cyrus (550 B.C.) to the conquest of Persia by Alexander the Great.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Zendavesta is a sacred books (of the ancient Persians)
q: Our knowledge of the religion of the ancient Persians is principally derived from the Zendavesta, or sacred books of that people.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddha is a mortal sage
q: Buddha, whom the Vedas represent as a delusive incarnation of Vishnu, is said by his followers to have been a mortal sage, whose name was Gautama, called also by the complimentary epithets of Sakyasinha, the Lion, and Buddha, the Sage.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddha has doctrines propagated all over India (so rapidly)
q: but his doctrines soon gained credit, and were propagated so rapidly that Buddha himself lived to see them spread all over India.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddha makes first converts Benares
q: At Benares he made his first converts, "turning the wheel of the law" for the first time.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddha converts his father
q: He converted great numbers, his father among the rest, but met with fierce opposition from the Hindu Scribes and Pharisees, the leading Brahmans.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddha dies at age eighty years
q: So he lived and taught, and died at the age of eighty years.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddha has discourses recorded in Buddhist sacred books
q: His discourses are contained in the sacred books of the Buddhists.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddha turns the wheel of the law (at Benares for the first time)
q: At Benares he made his first converts, "turning the wheel of the law" for the first time.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Vedas are rejected by Buddhism (entirely)
q: The Buddhists reject entirely the authority of the Vedas, and the religious observances prescribed in them and kept by the Hindus.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddhism is a religious sect
q: For several centuries after the appearance of Buddha, his sect seems to have been tolerated by the Brahmans, and Buddhism appears to have penetrated the peninsula of Hindustan in every direction, and to have been carried to Ceylon, and to the eastern peninsula.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddhism rejects the caste system
q: They also reject the distinction of castes, and prohibit all bloody sacrifices, and allow animal food.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddhism prohibits animal sacrifice (bloody sacrifices)
q: They also reject the distinction of castes, and prohibit all bloody sacrifices, and allow animal food.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddha has name Gautama
q: Buddha, whom the Vedas represent as a delusive incarnation of Vishnu, is said by his followers to have been a mortal sage, whose name was Gautama, called also by the complimentary epithets of Sakyasinha, the Lion, and Buddha, the Sage.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddhism is persecuted in India (for a long period, ultimately causing its abolition there)
q: But afterwards it had to endure in India a long continued persecution, which ultimately had the effect of entirely abolishing it in the country where it had originated, but to scatter it widely over adjacent countries.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddhism is introduced into China (about the year 65 of the Christian era)
q: Buddhism appears to have been introduced into China about the year 65 of our era.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Buddhism extends to Corea (from China)
q: From China it was subsequently extended to Corea, Japan, and Java.
